echoDetails.wallMotion: Normal global and regional wall motion

postRecord.title: Emergency Trauma & Hospitalization Report
postRecord.subtitle: Acute Trauma Resuscitation, Surgical Stabilization & Inpatient Management

accident.description: The patient reportedly fell from a motorcycle following a collision and sustained direct blunt trauma to the right thigh. He experienced immediate excruciating pain and inability to bear weight on the right lower limb. He was transported to the emergency department via trauma ambulance.

edAssessment.chiefComplaints: Severe right thigh pain, swelling, and inability to stand or walk. Pain aggravated by any limb movement.
edAssessment.circulation: Hemodynamically stable on initial triage assessment
edAssessment.externalBleeding: No significant active external bleeding reported
edAssessment.headInjury: No loss of consciousness reported; no obvious external head injury

physicalExam.rightLimb: Visible right thigh swelling, mid-thigh tenderness, gross deformity consistent with fracture and restricted movement due to severe pain. Closed injury: no open communicating wound or bone extrusion identified.
physicalExam.neurovascular: Distal pedal pulses (Dorsalis Pedis & Posterior Tibial) palpable; foot sensation and distal toe motor function fully preserved.
physicalExam.systemic: Chest examination clear; abdomen soft and non-tender; no focal neurological deficit identified.

radiology.investigation: Digital X-Ray Right Femur (AP and Lateral views)
radiology.findings: Displaced transverse fracture involving the midshaft of the right femur, with cortical disruption and displacement of fracture fragments. No additional fracture identified in visualized femur portions.
radiology.impression: Closed displaced transverse fracture of the midshaft of the right femur (AO/OTA 32-A3).
radiology.studyName: Digital X-Ray Right Femur (AP & Lateral Views)
radiology.priorComparison: No prior right femur radiograph on file; post-op CRIF nail alignment verified on 21 Nov 2026.

cardiacAssessment.ecgFindings: Sinus tachycardia, approximately 108 BPM. No acute ischemic ST-T changes identified. No sustained PSVT episode captured on the recorded ECG.
cardiacAssessment.monitoring: Continuous telemetry initiated due to known PSVT history. Cardiology review and anesthetic assessment cleared patient for operative fixation.

ecgDetails.intervals: PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 418 ms
ecgDetails.interpretation: Reactive sinus tachycardia secondary to acute trauma pain; no ST-T ischemic changes.

echoDetails.valveFindings: Trace physiological TR, structurally normal valves

events: Brief self-limiting sinus tachycardia (112 BPM) during immediate post-op recovery; no sustained PSVT

diagnosis.primary: Closed displaced transverse fracture of the midshaft right femur
diagnosis.secondary: Pre-existing paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT), stable during hospitalization
diagnosis.additional: Acute traumatic pain, localized soft-tissue swelling, and reactive sinus tachycardia

treatment.procedure: Closed reduction and internal fixation (CRIF) using an intramedullary interlocking nail
treatment.details: Operative stabilization under fluoroscopic guidance. Closed reduction achieved, insertion of right antegrade intramedullary nail with proximal and distal interlocking screws.
treatment.postopFindings: Acceptable anatomical alignment and satisfactory implant fixation. No immediate surgical complications. Distal neurovascular status preserved.

dischargeCondition.summary: Conscious and oriented; hemodynamically stable. No sustained cardiac arrhythmias during hospital stay. Surgical wound clean and dry; pain adequately controlled. Distal circulation and sensation intact.
dischargeCondition.mobility: Mobilization initiated with walker under physiotherapy supervision. Non-weight bearing on right lower limb.

followUp: Orthopedic review within 10–14 days for stitch removal and clinical assessment
Repeat right femur digital X-ray as advised
Wound inspection and dry dressing maintenance
Continue prescribed cardiac medication (Metoprolol 25mg QD) without interruption
Cardiology outpatient follow-up for PSVT monitoring
Follow prescribed 14-day subcutaneous thromboprophylaxis plan
Seek emergency medical evaluation if experiencing chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, or worsening leg pain
